facts: pidfd_open resolves the current numeric PID; it does not bind retrospectively to an earlier proc starttime/UID sample.
Poll readiness proves termination of the referenced process/thread group, not ownership, original starttime, parentage, reap-by-guard or descendant absence.
In inspected v6.8 fdinfo Pid:-1 means no attached PIDTYPE_PID task; Pid:0 may mean namespace visibility. Neither carries earlier starttime.
ECHILD can describe a live nonchild. WNOWAIT alone does not establish death or descendant closure.
Subreaper adoption depends on orphaning and the nearest living subreaper/namespace relationship; a live grandchild is not thereby waitable.
Unfrozen proc children reads can omit nonexiting children when another exits. Two equal running samples are not an atomic completeness guarantee.
sourceAssessment: Current C6 full identity/fdinfo/UID custody validation remains strict; historical terminal proof presupposes validated custody. READY census is sampled cooperative-fixture evidence, not kernel-guaranteed hostile graph closure.
recommendations: Preserve distinct validated-live, validated-terminal and unvalidated-acquisition-disappeared states; never promote the last into signalable custody, ACK or claimed reap.
No ENOENT/ESRCH or repeated-running-census waiver; require independently reviewed identity binding and descendant closure.
Model pre-open PID reuse, different live/dead referenced process, live nonchild/ECHILD, missing proc, namespace visibility, pre-custody orphaning and omitted surviving sibling.
Assess a quiescent or exclusively owned cgroup boundary with controlled migration/delegation/thaw/cleanup and actual aggregate observations.
limits: Inspected Linux v6.8 is not attestation of actual HOST kernel source/build.
SOURCE7 actual ENOENT/ESRCH does not prove exit/reap causation, PID reuse or strace child purpose.
